purpose: Preserve all primitive parallel charge branches in one PyMatching graph by replacing every physical branch with a private two-edge path through a zero-syndrome auxiliary detector.
epistemic_role: Bounded decoder-representation remediation only. It validates graph equivalence and branch identity before any sequential-policy risk is recomputed.

failed_prerequisite.finding: PyMatching 2.4.0 from_check_matrix collapses the twelve physical multigraph branches to six endpoint edges and retains only the minimum-weight fault id for each pair.
failed_prerequisite.bounded_matrix: Both colours, thirteen positive-weight profiles, and all eight even syndromes: 208 exhaustive comparisons have zero objective, boundary, minimizer-membership, or targeted-ID failures, but no matching graph retains both members of any parallel pair.
failed_prerequisite.consequence: The collapsed primitive graph returns a valid minimum-weight representative but is not topology-faithful enough to call the public second-stage decoder reproduced.

registered_adapter.branch_expansion: For physical branch e=(u,v), add private auxiliary a_e and edges (u,a_e) and (a_e,v). Give exactly one segment fault_id e and split the branch weight equally across the two segments.
registered_adapter.syndrome_embedding: Append twelve deterministic zero auxiliary syndrome bits to the four measured charge bits.
registered_adapter.equivalence_mechanism: The private auxiliary has degree two and zero syndrome, so any valid correction selects both branch segments or neither; the expanded path therefore has the original boundary, total weight, and one physical fault id.

required: all source hashes match the registration freeze
each colour produces exactly sixteen nodes, twenty-four graph edges, and twelve distinct fault ids in one matching object
every private auxiliary is incident only on its branch's two segments
the expanded syndrome has the measured four-bit charge syndrome followed by twelve zeros
for unit weights and every branch-forcing positive-weight profile, all eight even syndromes match exhaustive primitive objectives within 1e-6
every returned fault mask is an exhaustive minimum-weight primitive branch chain with the requested boundary
each branch-forcing profile selects its targeted branch and not its parallel twin on the pair-endpoint syndrome
returned branch sectors are computed with the validated linear period cochain
no sequential policy risk, stochastic sample, larger lattice, LER, threshold, or scalability claim is introduced
validation.fail_closed_rule: If the expanded graph admits a half-branch, loses a fault id, changes an exact objective, or returns a non-minimizing branch mask, stop before integrating it into the sequential policy audit.
